subject: Re: Performance SLOs & benchmark methodology - next steps
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-20T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Performance SLOs & benchmark methodology - follow up

Hi Marissa / Stephanie,

Thanks again for the call earlier — that was helpful. A quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can get a benchmark run scheduled: 

- Targets we care about: P95 latency <= 120ms for 1k token streaming responses; sustained throughput of ~150 req/s at 512 token average; concurrency up to 80 clients.
- Streaming: we need server-sent-chunk style streaming (partial tokens as they arrive) and want to validate end-to-end tail latency (first byte + completion).
- Reproducibility: we need a stable prompt set (mix of short/medium/long), deterministic seeds where applicable, and a clear harness that records hardware, model variant, quantization, and batching settings.

Can you share the benchmark harness and a proposed test plan (measurement definitions, prompt sets, run cadence)? Also let us know availability for a 2-hour test window next week.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of ML Ops, EdgeFin
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@edgefin.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-20T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & benchmark methodology - follow up

Hi Samir — great working with you today. Recap + next steps below.

Recap (brief):
- Redwood will validate streaming first-byte + completion latencies and end-to-end P50/P95/P99 for your target prompt mixes.
- We'll test the throughput target at 512-token avg and validate behavior at up to 80 concurrent clients.
- We'll include KV/prefix-caching disabled/enabled runs and two quantization profiles (fp16 and q4_0) so you can see tradeoffs.

Deliverables we will provide:
1) Benchmark harness (scripted runner + measurement collector)
2) Prompt set (short/medium/long) and seed file
3) Measurement definitions doc (latency types, how we measure streaming first-byte, sample rate, warm-up logic)
4) Run logs and reproducible artifact bundle (model config, kernel versions, hardware mapping)

Attached: benchmark-harness-v1.zip (runner + README), prompt-set-edgefin-v1.json (sample prompt set)
Attachment: benchmark-harness-v1.zip (zip, 12MB)
Attachment: prompt-set-edgefin-v1.json (json, 45KB)

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm a 2-hour window (we've got slots Mon-Fri next week 09:00-12:00 PT).
- We run baseline (fp16, no caching) + streaming latency test, then an optimized pass (q4_0 + caching) if you want.
- We'll share the raw artifacts + a short writeup with graphs and pass/fail vs your targets.

Question for you: do you want us to push test results into your S3/GCS bucket or upload to a shared Drive?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Measurement defs and runner notes (internal)

Marissa / Steph — leaving a quick internal note on measurement definitions I suggest we include in the deliverable. Adding these as bullet items we can drop into the doc.

- Latency types:
  * First-byte (time from request started to first chunk received) — measured on client side with wall clock and server-side trace for correlation.
  * Completion (time from request start to final token) — wall clock.
  * Token throughput (tokens/sec delivered) and per-request tokens/sec.
- Sampling: 10% of requests recorded with full traces, full histogram for all requests for Pxx calculation.
- Warmup: 60s at 20% target RPS before measurement window.
- Concurrency model: emulate 80 concurrent clients with randomized inter-arrival times matching your production traffic distribution (we'll need the real hist if available).
- Streaming verification: measure time-to-first-byte and also first 100ms/500ms delivery chunk sizes.

Also: ensure we tag all runs with model git commit / kernel selector string. I can attach a short runner script snippet to the harness.

—Dylan
From: Samir Patel <samir@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-21T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & benchmark methodology - follow up

Thanks Marissa — that looks good. A couple clarifications before we lock the window: 

1) For streaming first-byte, we need the client-side measurement to include TLS handshake + DNS (we want end-user observed first-byte). Can you confirm the harness is capturing that?
2) On concurrency emulation: we can provide a sample production inter-arrival distribution and a small load agent (we prefer k6 for distribution). Will your runner integrate with a k6 script or should we convert?
3) For reproducibility, please include the exact CUDA / kernel versions and full model checkpoint sha in the artifact bundle.

We can do Tue 2026-02-24 10:00-12:00 PT for the 2-hour window. Prefer results uploaded to the shared Drive link (see below).

Shared Drive (EdgeFin): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEDGEFIN-BENCH

Thanks — Samir
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-22T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & benchmark methodology - next steps

Samir — perfect, thanks for the clarifications. Quick answers and final plan below.

Answers:
- TLS/DNS: the harness runs client-side agents that perform full TCP/TLS handshake and DNS resolution by default; we'll surface both pure server-side timings and end-to-end (client-observed) timings in the report.
- k6: we have a k6-compatible loader in the harness already (we use a thin adapter). Please send your inter-arrival distribution (csv) and we'll drop it into the k6 script.
- Repro bundle: we'll include CUDA runtime, driver, kernel selector string, and model checkpoint sha (and note quantization steps).

Confirmed test window: Tue 2026-02-24 10:00-12:00 PT — Redwood will run baseline + streaming latency pass. Deliverables will be uploaded to the shared Drive link you provided.

Checklist for run day:
- EdgeFin to provide: inter-arrival distribution csv, S3/GCS creds if you want artifact copy to your cloud, and any IP allowlist for test agents.
- Redwood to provide: harness bundle (attached earlier), measurement-defs doc, run plan and tagging scheme.

Shared links:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4821
- Harness repo snapshot: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness/tree/edgefin

We'll prepare a short run-notes template and send it by EOD Monday. Looking forward to the test.

Best,
Marissa
